For the State : A.P.P.

04/Dated: 02/01/2019 Sole petitioner has preferred this criminal revision application, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the order dated 27.03.2003 passed by Shri Rameshwar Rai, learned 5 th Additional Sessions Judge,
Hazaribagh in Cr. Appeal No. 138 of 1991, whereby and whereunder the appellate court has dismissed the appeal and affirming the judgment of conviction dated 29.06.1991 passed by the Sri.
H.P. Singh, learned J.M., Hazaribagh,

in G.R. Case No. 214 of 1987, T.R. No. 190 of 1991, convicted the petitioner under Section 16 (1) A (I) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced him for a period of one year and to pay a fine of Rs. 1000/- and in default of payment of fine to undergo R.I. for three months.

It appears that the criminal revision was filed on 31.07.2003 and under order dated 16.08.2003, the appeal was admitted for hearing and L.C.R. was called for and petitioner was admitted on bail and only after a period of 16 years, it is listed today.

Learned counsel for the petitioner while assailing the judgment of both the courts below has submitted that both the courts have not considered Exhibit - 8, which is sanctioned order granted by Chief Medical Officer, Mines Board, Hazaribagh and relying on the judgment reported in the case of State of Maharastra Vs. Gopal Prasad Govind Prasad Agrawal, 1999 Cr.L.J. 468 has further Ashok Chouhan vs The State Of Jharkhand .....

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Opp. ...
on 2 January, 2019

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112181387/
1 submitted that from perusal of Exhibit-8, it reveals that the Sanction Authority has failed to apply his judicial mind and has given sanction in mechanical manner which vitiated the entire trial, but it was not considered by learned SDJM and learned appellate court.
So, both the courts have failed to exercise their jurisdiction vested upon them.
So, the judgments passed by both the courts below are fit to be set aside and the instant criminal revision is fit to be allowed.

The relevant portion of the aforesaid judgment reads as under:
Requirement of section fulfilled:- The orders show that the Joint Commissioner,
Food and Drug, Pune Division (the consenting authority) had gone through the relevant reocrds of the cases including the reports of the Public Analyst and he specifically recorded therein that the prosecution against the appellants were called for the alleged offences committed.
The orders granting consent fulfill all the requirement of Section 20 of the Act.
Learned APP is directed to reply on this point.
Let the name of Mr. Nehru Mahto, APP be reflected in the cause list on behalf of the State.
List this case on 05.02.2019.
Let a copy of order be handed over to Mr. Nehru Mahto, learned APP.

(Anant Bijay Singh, J.) Sunil/
